key_insight: Machine-learning models can accurately predict band gaps across diverse lead-free halide perovskite families using simple atomic and structural descriptors.
engineering_relevance: These predictions can speed up screening of new perovskite compositions by highlighting which B-site and X-site properties most strongly control band gap design.
method: Trained ensemble tree-based regressors on atomic and structural descriptors.
Compared random forest regression, gradient boosted regression trees, and XGBoost.
Used feature-importance analysis to identify dominant band-gap drivers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive accuracy across multiple halide perovskite types and uses feature importance to link model performance to physically meaningful descriptors.
watch_item: Model reliability may depend on the diversity and size of the training data, so extrapolation to unseen chemistries should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites
